Subject: Sponsor top-up: can credits be pooled across cohort companies?

Hi Priyom,

Quick one — we run an accelerator and want to apply a single sponsor top-up (USD 75k) across three portfolio companies that LaunchFoundry sponsors in your accelerator. The ask from our ops team: instead of issuing three separate credit allocations to individual accounts, can Redwood issue a single sponsor credit that LaunchFoundry redeems and allocates internally OR allow us to net that sponsor credit against a monthly invoice across the three accounts?

Attached is a short note from our finance team (LF-PO-9876) that outlines the portfolio list and expected timing.

Key constraints: we need the credits to be visible for accounting and ideally have a paper trail (invoice/PO). Can you confirm policy on: 1) commingling sponsor credits across multiple customer accounts; 2) whether credits can be applied as a negative line item on a single invoice; and 3) any procurement or tax implications Redwood needs to consider?

We'd like to close this before the next cohort kickoff (June 10).

Thanks — happy to hop on a quick call.

Priyom / Ben — reviewed the PO (LF-PO-9876) and the request. Short answer: we can support the economics but there are accounting and contractual nuances. Notes below: 

1) Accounting visibility: ADA-friendly approach is to issue one invoice to LaunchFoundry for the sponsor top-up, and then create three separate internal credit allocations tied to each beneficiary customer account. This preserves per-account visibility in our billing system and keeps sponsor funds traceable for revenue recognition.

2) Commingling (one credit retained by Redwood and applied across multiple accounts on demand) is technically possible but creates complications: 
- It blurs the linkage between sponsor funds and customer usage for GAAP and our audit trail (SOC2 / revenue sub-ledgers).
- It complicates refund/chargeback handling if one beneficiary churns or over-uses.
- Tax: issuing a single negative line on an invoice that offsets multiple legal entities we don't formally bill is risky unless we have a Purchase Order and remit path for each legal entity.

3) Practical compromise we can offer (fast path): 
- Redwood invoices LaunchFoundry for USD 75,000 (net 30) as a sponsorship payment.
- Upon payment, finance issues three named credits (25k each) attached to the beneficiary accounts. We will provide an accounting worksheet and a final invoice record showing the allocation (so you can attach to your internal ledger).

4) Alternate (if LaunchFoundry insists on single-invoice netting): we can allow the sponsor to prepay and we will create a ledger-level credit in LaunchFoundry's sponsor account; however, this will be marked as restricted sponsor funds and we will require a signed Sponsor Credit Agreement (simple addendum) that clarifies redemption rules and refund policy. This adds ~2–3 business days for legal and docs.

Recommendation: if they want speed (cohort starts June 10), go with the fast path — invoice + three named credits. If they need centralized control, sign the addendum and we'll route through our sponsor ledger (but anticipate extra steps).

I've attached a draft invoice and a short sponsor-addendum template we can use. Ben — can you handle the sales-side language for the addendum and confirm any discounts we want to offer for multi-cohort commitments?

—Mina
